messages:
maria: FYI support ticket #1234 — AcmeCorp hitting p99 spikes on /v1/generate since the 03:20 deploy. They report tail latency > 2.5s and saw a sharp increase exactly at deploy time. I see prefix/KV cache miss rate jump ~10x in the same window. Any quick theories?

ops-bot: ALERT: prod text-gen p99 exceeded 2.0s for 7m (03:22–03:29). Affected routes: /v1/generate. Related traces: https://traces.internal/acme/1234.

samir: I pulled a few traces. Looks like a ton of cache-key churn for the prefix cache — different keys observed that should have been normalized. Example: tenant header contains "X-Tenant: acme-us" but normalization code uses raw prompt hash + raw prefix so any small metadata change makes new key.

jess: Can you paste an example request/keys from the trace? also curious if eviction rates jumped too.

samir: pasted trace snippet:
```
prefix_key: "acme-us||/product/desc||prompt_v2||len:64||user:123"
prefix_key: "acme-us||/product/desc||prompt_v2||len:64||user:123|region:eu"
prefix_key: "acme-us|/product/desc|prompt_v2|len:64|user:123"
```
You can see small delimiter differences and extra tags. Normalization used to collapse to a canonical 6-token tuple but a refactor removed the canonicalizer in favour of a "fast concat" path.

devin: Oof. That explains cardinality explosion. Cache hotset spilled, continuous evictions => warmup storm => increased p95/p99. Short-term mitigations: 1) flip feature flag to re-enable canonical normalizer, 2) enable per-tenant cache tagging so evictions don't evict every tenant's hot keys, 3) throttle warmup to use jittered splay.

maria: Ops, can we toggle the flag and throttle warmup? If rollback is risky, feature toggle is preferred. Customer needs immediate relief. :pray:

ops-bot: infractl run --env prod feature toggle prefix_canonicalizer --off
ops-bot: NOTE: toggling will take ~30s to propagate to runtime nodes, watch for 03:35–03:36.

jess: I also recommend adding a short-term circuit breaker for requests that produce > 100 unique prefix keys per minute per connection — return 429 with Retry-After if exceeded. That should stop stampede.

samir: Agreed. I'll PR a quick patch to re-introduce the canonical path and add a small fuzz-proof normalizer (strip extra tags, unify delimiters). Patch preview:
```
# previous: key = "|".join(parts)
# new: key = f"{tenant}:{space}:{bucket}:{shorthash}"  # canonicalized
parts = sanitize(parts)  # strip empty/ordering-insignificant tags
key = ":".join(parts[:4]) + ":" + short_hash(relevant_payload)
```
I'll push to canary once flag is off.

devin: For cache policy, ops: can we bump the prefix cache min-reserved size by 20% while we stabilize? Also consider switching eviction from pure LRU to an LFU-ish decayed frequency (or CLOCK) to preserve high-use short-lived keys.

ops-bot: Command to update config: infractl memcache update --name prefix_cache --min-reserved 1.2x --eviction-policy CLOCK
ops-bot: Applying change now to prod staging ring 1.

maria: Support: let customer know we've toggled canonicalizer and are applying cache-policy tweaks. Offer a short-term mitigation: route heavy tenants to dedicated nodes if they keep hitting spikes.

support-bot: Ticket #1234 updated: "We've applied a normalization toggle and cache policy changes. Asking you to verify latency in next 10 minutes. If you still see issues, please share recent trace IDs." :email:

jess: Repro steps for ops/dev to validate locally:
1) run local server build with noisy-key-mode on (env NOISY_KEYS=1).
2) replay sample request set: `python tools/replay_traces.py --trace sample_acme.json --rate 50`
3) watch prefix miss metric: `metrics query prefix_cache.miss_rate{env:local}`

samir: Also added some dashboards and alerts: prefix_cardinality_p95, prefix_eviction_rate_p90. Query examples added to the ticket.

maria: TL;DR root cause: accidental removal of canonicalization path in prefix key code -> key entropy increase -> cache thrash -> warmup storms -> p99 spike. Short term: toggled canonicalizer flag, bumped cache reservation, applied CLOCK eviction, added circuit breaker. Medium term: revert refactor with proper tests, add integration test for key cardinality, and implement staggered warmup with jittered splay (to avoid stampedes on large fleets).

devin: I'll own the medium-term changes with samir. Samir will open the rollback/patch PR and add tests. Ops will monitor for 30m and then we’ll consider resizing or dedicated routing if Acme still needs it.

maria: Thanks all — customer pinged: latencies back to normal for now. Closing loop in 1h unless regressions. :tada:
